confidence_notes: I checked three cost-of-living aggregators for food and drink: Numbeo (April 2026), Livingcost (June 2026) and Wise. Their figures differ by a factor of two or more, partly because the Argentine peso is volatile. Restaurant figures are the midpoint of Numbeo's higher numbers and Livingcost's lower ones. Inexpensive meals ranged from about 13 to 25 USD and mid-range dinners for two from about 40 to 60 USD. Cappuccino ranged from about 3 to 6 USD and a pub beer from about 3.3 to 6 USD. I found no reliable aggregated prices for cocktails or wine by the glass in Ushuaia. Those two were estimated from their usual price relationship to beer in Argentine tourist towns, so they are less certain. Accommodation figures come from general knowledge, not live listings. July is winter ski season (Cerro Castor), which is shoulder to high demand, and Ushuaia's remote location keeps rooms more expensive than in most Argentine cities. The FX figure is the latest RBA observation available on the generation date and was not taken in July 2026.
comparable_city_reasoning: Patagonian tourist towns with similar remoteness and tourism demand were used for comparison: El Calafate and Bariloche in Argentina, and Punta Arenas in Chile, which Expatistan rates about 7% more expensive than Ushuaia. Ushuaia's prices sit at the high end for Argentina.
